title: NSDR for Severe Recovery Deficit
description: Sleep duration, HRV, and resting heart rate have all moved sharply against your personal baseline — a severe, high-confidence recovery deficit. Recommends an extended NSDR session and postponing intense training for the day.

conditional.question: Your sleep, HRV, and resting heart rate all look significantly off from your baseline today — is that accurate?

actions.frequency: Once, on the day this triggers (repeat if it persists)
actions.timing: Morning, with an optional second short session in the evening
actions.details: A longer guided NSDR or Yoga Nidra session, potentially split across the day, to maximize parasympathetic recovery support given the severity of the signal.

actions.frequency: Once, on the day this triggers
actions.details: Postpone planned high-intensity, heavy-load, or long-duration training. Prefer full rest or very light activity (short walk, gentle mobility). Reassess against the next night's data before resuming normal intensity.

benefits: Avoids training through a severe, multi-signal-confirmed autonomic strain state
Reduces risk of illness, injury, or prolonged recovery debt from pushing through this state
Extended NSDR provides a larger relative recovery benefit at this severity than the high-tier dose
science: This tier uses the same three-signal logic as the high-recovery-deficit rule (sleep duration, HRV, resting heart rate all deviating from personal baseline in the same night) but at tighter thresholds, reflecting a more severe deviation. The wider gap from baseline across all three concurrently-monitored systems increases confidence that this represents genuine, not noise-driven, autonomic strain.
contraindications: If this state recurs on consecutive days, this is a stronger signal to consult a physician or coach rather than repeatedly self-managing with NSDR alone

Not a diagnosis of illness — if accompanied by other symptoms (fever, sore throat, unusual fatigue), treat as a possible early illness signal and prioritize rest/medical guidance over training decisions

learning_resources.title: Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR) — Huberman Lab official page

evidence_metadata.scientific_rationale: Same three-signal design as the high tier (sleep duration, HRV, resting HR vs. personal baseline, 1 night), with tighter thresholds (80%/80%/110%) intended to isolate a more severe subset of recovery-deficit nights that warrant postponing rather than merely reducing training.

evidence_for_protocol.notes: Same as the high tier: NSDR as a recovery-support tool and avoiding intense training during genuine autonomic strain are both directly supported by Huberman Lab source material.

evidence_for_trigger.notes: The tightened 80%/80%/110% thresholds are a product heuristic — a reasonable escalation from the high tier's 85%/85%/105% but not derived from any cited study establishing that these specific cutoffs mark a qualitatively different (rather than merely quantitatively worse) state. Persistence is kept at 1 night to match the brief's worked example exactly; an alternative design worth testing later is requiring persistence >= 2 nights before recommending postponing training outright, since a single severe night could still be one-off noise (illness onset, travel, alcohol, etc.) rather than accumulated strain — flagged here rather than implemented, to avoid silently diverging from the brief's spec.

expected_effect.short_term: Meaningfully reduced same-day physiological load; NSDR dose is larger than the high tier to match the larger deficit.
expected_effect.long_term: Intended to prevent the worst-case outcome of training through severe strain (illness, injury, prolonged recovery), though, like the high tier, this exact rule has not been outcome-tested.
